en_US.audio: A creature card earns its place by changing the route.
en_US.in_game_wiki: Ecology Scan Evidence Rule separates useful specimen cards from decorative bestiary entries.
en_US.external_site: HECTON-8 ecology matters when it changes navigation, sound, oxygen, pressure or evidence.
en_US.field_note: Codex anchors belong near physical behavior, not menu-only lists.

en_US.title: Final Descent Evidence Rule
en_US.scanner: Final-descent anchors: machine field warning, pressure gate, factory-temple, payload check.
en_US.terminal: FINAL-DESCENT ANCHORS: warning, gate, threshold, and payload authority come before optional late archive fragments.
en_US.audio: The bottom should ask through instruments first.
en_US.in_game_wiki: Final Descent Evidence Rule preserves engineering pressure before the final question.
en_US.external_site: The final approach should feel like a machine refusing simple categories, not a boss arena.
en_US.field_note: Atlas basin anchors take priority only after warning, pressure gate, threshold, and payload authority are bound.

en_US.title: Terminal Evidence Triage Rule
en_US.scanner: Terminal anchors come first when they alter route, proof, or ending record.
en_US.terminal: TRIAGE: promote terminal anchors only when they change route judgement, prove a lie, unlock a table/card, or affect ending record context.
en_US.audio: A terminal earns power by changing the next decision.
en_US.in_game_wiki: Terminal Evidence Triage Rule keeps terminal records from becoming walls of detached text.
en_US.external_site: HECTON-8 terminals work best when the player is already holding a broken part or a bad route warning.
en_US.field_note: A terminal earns placement only when it changes a decision, proves a lie, unlocks a record, or affects an ending context.
